chunks.text: Today we will talk about Venezuela.
Venezuela is a colorful, warm, and diverse country in South America.
Let's learn about it in slow and easy English.
Where is Venezuela?
Venezuela is in the north of South America.
It is next to Columbia, Brazil, and Guyana.
To the north, it touches the Caribbean Sea.
It has mountains, jungles, plains, and beaches.
What is the capital city of Venezuela?
The capital city is Caracas.
Caracas is a busy, large, and modern city.
It has museums, markets, mountains, and traffic.
It is the biggest city in the country.
Other cities include Maracaibo near a big lake, Valencia, an important industrial city, Merida in the Andes Mountains, Ciudad Bolívar near the Orinoco River.
How many people live in Venezuela?
About 28 million people live in Venezuela.
Most people live in cities, especially near the north coast.
The country has many ethnic groups and cultures.
What language do people speak in Venezuela?
The official language is Spanish.
People speak it with a Caribbean accent.
In some areas, people also speak indigenous languages, such as Guayu and Pemón.
Some also speak a little English or Portuguese.
What is the weather like in Venezuela?
Venezuela has a tropical climate.
It is hot all year, especially in the lowlands.
There are wet and dry seasons.
In the mountains, the weather is cooler.
In the Amazon, it is hot and rainy.
What does Venezuela look like?
Venezuela has many landscapes.
Mountains, the Andes are in the west.
The Yanos, wide, flat grasslands.
The Orinoco River, one of the longest in South America.
Rain forests, waterfalls and beaches.
It is home to Angel Falls, the tallest waterfall in the world.
What animals live in Venezuela?
Venezuela has many wild animals.
Jaguars, monkeys and anteaters.
Anacondas, frogs and turtles.
Crocodiles and pink river dolphins.
Parrots, toucan birds and eagles.
The Amazon rainforest in the south is full of wildlife.
What do people eat in Venezuela?
Venezuelan food is tasty, filling and made with corn and meat.
People eat arepas, round corn cakes with cheese, meat or eggs.
Pabellón criollo, rice with black beans, beef and plantains.
Empanadas, fried pastries with many fillings.
Halacas, a Christmas dish with meat and corn dough wrapped in leaves.
Cachapas, sweet corn pancakes with cheese.
Many meals include rice, plantains, yucca and avocados.
What do people drink in Venezuela?
People drink coffee, very popular and strong.
Fruit juice like passion fruit, guava or mango.
Chicha, a sweet rice milk drink.
Coconut water and cold soda.
Adults may drink rum, beer or aguardiente.
Drinks are often served cold because of the hot weather.
What is life like in Venezuela?
Life in Venezuela is often lively, family -based and musical.
People enjoy spending time with family and neighbors.
Cooking and eating together.
Dancing to salsa, merengue and reggaeton.
Going to the beach or visiting the mountains.
Watching baseball, the most popular sport.
People are known for their warmth and hospitality.
What are some holidays and traditions?
Independence Day, July 5th.
Carnival with music, costumes and parades.
Christmas and New Year with food and fireworks.
Holy Week, Samana Santa, a religious holiday.
Gaeta and Joropo, traditional music styles.
Venezuelans love to celebrate, dance and share food.
Some fun facts about Venezuela.
Venezuela means little Venice in Spanish.
It has huge oil reserves.
Angel Falls is 979 meters tall.
The flag is yellow, blue and red with stars.
Venezuela has snowy mountains, jungles and beaches all in one country.
Now you know many things about Venezuela.
You know where it is, what people eat and how they live.
You learned about Angel Falls, Arepas and Caribbean music.
Well done.
Thank you for listening to the Slow English Podcast.
I am Emili.
